# live-state-snapshot

<!-- AUTOGENERATED:BEGIN — do not edit; regenerated by `./singularity build` -->

## Plugin reference

- Description: L2 persisted live-state materialization: durable snapshot + xmin watermark for instant cold boot, served only from a usable row (a key the runtime persists now, under its current definition, from a current writer). Two persist modes (a FULL recompute replaces; a persisted alias's trailing window lowers the floor), an hourly compact job, and a boot catch-up that seeds each persisted alias from its row and replays the changelog by scope — or, when history was pruned past the floor or a rollup was healed, recomputes every persisted key.
- Server:
  - Contributes: `fork-data-exclusion` "live_state_snapshot"
  - Uses:
    - `database.db`
    - `database/admin.ExcludeFromFork`
    - `database/change-feed.producedTableNames`
    - `database/change-feed.readLayout`
    - `database/change-feed.routeChange`
    - `database/derived-tables.reconciledRollups`
    - `infra/jobs.defineJob`
    - `primitives/log-channels.defineLogSink`
  - DB schema: `plugins/database/plugins/live-state-snapshot/server/internal/tables-ddl.ts`
  - Exports (types): `ReadSetShrinkEvent`
  - Exports (values):
    - `clearPersistedSnapshots`
    - `onReadSetShrink`
    - `readPersistedSnapshots`
    - `reconcileReadSetTable`
  - Register:
    - `defineJob('database.live-state-changelog-prune')`
    - `defineJob('live-state-snapshot.compact')`
- Cross-plugin:
  - Imported by:
    - `debug/profiling/boot-bench`

## The usable-row predicate (A18 / C22 / C23)

Every L2 read — the boot snapshot, the boot seed, the usable check, catch-up's
floor, the compact job's targets — serves only a USABLE row (`usableRowSql`):

```
resource_key = ANY($persisted)                       -- persistedKeys(), C23
AND definition IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ($defs::jsonb ->> resource_key)   -- A18
AND definition_at IS NOT DISTINCT FROM persisted_at  -- C22
```

The expectation (`L2Expectation`, `./internal/expectation.ts`) is the running
runtime's own answer: the keys it persists right now (a bounded or external
key's leftover row is never served, whatever a previous boot left) and each
one's definition (`persistedDefinitions()`, a routed plan's SQL fingerprint;
absent ⇒ NULL). `definition_at` has NO default: every writer that knows the
column stamps it with the same `now()` as `persisted_at`, so an older backend's
upsert during a hot swap — which moves `persisted_at` and not `definition_at` —
leaves a row that invalidates itself instead of carrying the new definition over
an old value. Rows from before the columns existed fail once (the intended
one-time recompute). The boot sweep (`sweepUnusableSnapshots`) deletes every
unusable row; the reads refuse them regardless.

## Persist modes

The runtime's hook (`persistSnapshot(db, key, pk, value, watermark, meta)`) has two
modes (see resource-runtime's *L2 persists*):

- **`replace`** (a FULL recompute) writes the value, `position` = the flight's
  watermark, `position_at = now()`, `tables_read` = the run's read-set and the
  definition;
- **`floor`** (a persisted alias's trailing window) writes the value and LOWERS
  `position` to the snapshot's base floor (`LEAST`), keeping `position_at` and
  `tables_read`; a missing row is inserted with the floor, `meta.guardTables` and a
  NULL `position_at` — and so is a row this writer could not use (another
  definition's, or an older writer's upsert), whose read-set and replace time are
  someone else's: it is not re-validated with them under this definition.

The A6 guard (`./produced-guard`) judges `meta.guardTables` in both modes (C21) —
never an empty list, so a floor persist's first INSERT of a key reading a
produced table is refused too.

## Compaction (`live-state-snapshot.compact`)

Hourly at `:30` (offset from the changelog prune at `:00`), per worktree,
singleton, `instant`. A floor persist never raises a row's position and an idle
legacy key never re-persists, while catch-up and the prune both read the GLOBAL
`min(position)` — so every persisted key without a usable row REPLACED in the last
hour (`position_at`; a missing, unusable or floor-only row counts) is
`recomputeResource`d here, which replaces its row with a fresh floor. It runs in
the serving backend (a per-worktree job), where `recomputeResource` is in-process.

## Boot flow

`onReadyBlocking` first asserts the boot schema layer committed
(derived-tables' `reconciledRollups()`, A20 — `database` is a dependsOn edge, so
it always has; a throw there is a boot-order bug). When that layer's reconcile
**healed** a rollup, `initSnapshotSubsystem` clears every persisted row
(`clearHealedSnapshots`) before the read-set seed and before readiness flips,
so boot-snapshot's first read can never serve a value computed from the
drifted rollup as a first paint. For the same reason it then clears every
persisted alias row whose value does not parse as its entry's payload (A30,
`clearInvalidAliasSnapshots` over the runtime's `validatePersistedValue`):
boot-snapshot's persisted fast path is open from readiness, while `onReady`'s
seed has not yet put a kept snapshot in front of the row, and the client's
hydrate would reject such a value on every page load.

`onReady` (after the LISTEN is up) runs `runBootCatchUp` (`./internal/boot-catch-up.ts`),
in this order:

0. **a rollup the boot reconcile healed** (`reconciledRollups()`, rows upserted or
   deleted) → the backstop below: a heal rewrites rollup rows with nothing in the
   changelog (rollups are feed-exempt) and a reader may reach a rollup through a
   view, so no persisted value can be proven current. The rows were already
   cleared in `onReadyBlocking`; they are cleared again (a previous backend may
   have persisted one in between) and every key recomputes. A clean boot heals
   nothing (the reconcile is diff-first), so this is rare;
1. read the usable rows' read-sets;
2. `probeCatchUp` — the floor is the oldest USABLE row's position;
3. **backstop** (the prune horizon ≥ the floor: the prune deleted history at or
   after it) → clear the persisted rows, `recomputeResource` every persisted key,
   and stop — nothing is seeded from a row that cannot be proven current, and
   nothing is replayed;
4. otherwise: force-FULL-recompute every persisted key with no usable read-set;
   **seed** each persisted `scopedMembership` alias's in-memory diff base from its
   usable L2 row (`seedPersistedSnapshot(key, "{}", value, { position, positionAt })`
   — the row's position becomes the snapshot's base floor) so the first post-boot
   change is a scoped refill, not a FULL O(collection) rebuild; then replay from the
   LOWER of the probe's floor and every seeded row's position (`replayCatchUp`).
   Seeding runs BEFORE the replay on purpose — the missed-changes replay then also
   goes scoped. The seed rows are read after the probe, and during a hot swap the
   previous backend may floor-persist in between, lowering a row below the probe's
   floor — hence the min; a seeded row the changelog was pruned past is recomputed
   instead of seeded, as the backstop would. **A30:** the runtime parses the value
   against the alias's payload schema before seeding it; a value that does not
   parse (`{ kind: "invalid" }` — a row schema moved in a way the definition does
   not fingerprint) is treated as a missing row: logged, its row cleared (so
   boot-snapshot stops serving it) and the key recomputed. The barrier sweep
   above already cleared such rows; this is the backstop.

`onShutdown` drops the armed trailing floor persists (`dropPendingPersists`): their
changes are in the changelog and each row's floor still predates them.

Catch-up replays each changelog row EXACTLY as the live listener would (its
invariant), so it **preserves `row.ids` for every op** — a `D`-with-ids stays a cheap
scoped membership exit (zero loader queries), not a FULL. Only a genuinely null-ids
bulk statement degrades to FULL. A routed table's row also carries its key layout
(`keys`, row-wise jsonb) and known-unchanged column set (`unchanged`), written by the routed
trigger with the post-cap values it NOTIFYs; the replay reads them by the
listener's own rule (change-feed's `readLayout`), so a routed resource's replay is
as scoped as the live path, and a layout that does not parse routes unscoped
(FULL for its readers), reported — never dropped — on both paths. Both replay as
written: `unchanged` names only columns KNOWN equal in every row, a fact
whatever gate the trigger compared under, so a replay after a deploy that
changed the routes still reaches a route reading a column the old gate did not
compare; a column the old layout did not carry reads `keys` as unknown, which
recomputes rather than skips.

## The prune horizon (`live_state_changelog_horizon`)

The hourly prune (`pruneChangelog`) deletes `xid < min(position)` or rows past a
24 h ceiling, and in the SAME statement moves a one-row horizon to the highest
xid it deleted (never down). Catch-up judges every floor by that horizon
(`isPrunedPast`: horizon ≥ position). Never by the oldest RETAINED xid: the
changelog is sparse, so after an ordinary prune its oldest survivor sits above
the floor with nothing missing in between — that rule cleared and recomputed
every persisted key on every boot after a prune. Only the ceiling can delete at
or after a floor. A missing row is seeded with the most that could have been
pruned (below the oldest retained row; the current xid for an empty changelog;
NULL with no changelog yet).

## Invariant harness (DB-backed)

`persist.ts` and `catch-up.ts` are **db-parametrized** (they take
`db: NodePgDatabase`, no `@plugins/database/server` singleton import) so the real
SQL can be exercised against a throwaway Postgres. The `db` singleton is bound only
in the backend entry `server/index.ts` (hooks + catch-up) and in
`internal/public-snapshots.ts` (the two barrel-exported consumers keep their
`(keys) => …` shape).

- `server/internal/persist.test.ts` — the persist SQL: `captureWatermark` xid8
  monotonicity, both persist modes (replace in place; floor `LEAST`, kept
  `position_at` / `tables_read`, first INSERT, and a row another definition or
  an older writer left taken over as a missing one), the `text[]` / jsonb round-trips,
  the usable-row predicate on every read (a non-persisted key, another
  definition, the C22 old-shape upsert after a new-shape one), the compact
  targets, the boot sweep, `clearPersistedSnapshots` scoped delete.
- `server/internal/catch-up.test.ts` — the cold-boot arithmetic with a recording
  `route` spy: `probeCatchUp`'s verdict (`none` / `backstop` / `replay`, the floor
  over usable rows only; an ordinary prune below the floor is no backstop), the
  prune horizon (recorded by the real prune, never lowered, seeded when missing), `xid >= floor` + `ORDER BY seq` replay, the floor
  boundary (`==` in, `-1` out), id-preserving replay (a `D`-with-ids keeps its ids
  → scoped on the live path; only a genuinely null-ids row degrades to FULL),
  "already current", and a routed row's `keys` and `unchanged` replayed as
  written (a malformed layout unscoped, never dropped).
- `server/internal/boot-catch-up.test.ts` — the `onReady` order with the runtime
  calls recorded: a backstop boot — and a boot whose reconcile healed a rollup —
  clears the rows and recomputes every persisted key (nothing seeded or replayed);
  `clearHealedSnapshots` leaves boot-snapshot's read nothing to serve after a heal
  and touches nothing after a clean boot; a normal boot recomputes the unusable keys,
  seeds each usable alias at its row's position, then replays — from a seeded
  row's position when another writer lowered it after the probe, and with that
  alias recomputed instead when it was lowered past the prune horizon; an alias
  whose value the runtime refuses to seed (A30) has its row cleared and is
  recomputed, never seeded; `clearInvalidAliasSnapshots` (the `onReadyBlocking`
  A30 sweep) clears only the persisted alias rows whose value fails the parse
  (never a non-alias or non-persisted key's), and `onReady` then recomputes
  that key instead of seeding it.

The shared `db-test-fixture` primitive (`createTestDb`) provisions an isolated
throwaway database via admin's public barrel and drops it after. **Running:** needs a running cluster —
`./singularity test plugins/database/plugins/live-state-snapshot` (the fixture throws loudly
if the cluster is unreachable). Nothing has to be set in the environment: the
root `bunfig.toml` `[test]` preload (`test/bun-preload.ts`) declares the current
checkout as the test process's runtime namespace. See
`research/2026-07-03-database-live-state-db-backed-invariant-harness.md`.
